title: Urgency and Social Engineering — The Psychology of Scams
publisher: Cyber Dost, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
text: Financial scams rely heavily on psychological manipulation rather than technical hacking. The most effective tactic is creating artificial urgency to prevent the victim from thinking clearly or consulting others. Common urgency phrases used in Indian scams: 'Your account will be blocked in 2 hours', 'Last chance — offer expires at midnight', 'Act now or face a legal case', 'Cyber Crime Branch has flagged your number', 'Your electricity will be cut in 1 hour unless you pay now', 'Claim your refund before it expires today'. These statements are designed to trigger panic and bypass rational decision-making. Other social engineering tactics: (1) Authority impersonation — pretending to be from RBI, NPCI, Income Tax, Cyber Crime, TRAI, or a bank. Official agencies do not demand immediate payments via UPI or phone. (2) Fear of arrest or penalty — no government agency in India arrests people for not updating KYC or for a 'suspicious number'. (3) Sympathy manipulation — 'I'm stuck in the hospital, please send money urgently.' Always verify independently. The golden rule: If a message or call makes you feel panicked and pressured to act immediately, pause. Legitimate organisations give time. Take 10 minutes to call a trusted person or the official helpline before doing anything.
